concepts.name: is_spring
concepts.description: Forecast period falls in spring (March, April, May).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return seg.get('time_context', {}).get('season') == 'spring'

concepts.name: is_summer
concepts.description: Forecast period falls in summer (June, July, August).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return seg.get('time_context', {}).get('season') == 'summer'

concepts.name: is_autumn
concepts.description: Forecast period falls in autumn (September, October, November).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return seg.get('time_context', {}).get('season') == 'autumn'

concepts.name: is_winter
concepts.description: Forecast period falls in winter (December, January, February).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return seg.get('time_context', {}).get('season') == 'winter'

concepts.name: is_morning
concepts.description: Forecast window starts in the morning (hour 5-10).

concepts.name: is_midday
concepts.description: Forecast window starts in the midday range (hour 11-15).

concepts.name: is_evening
concepts.description: Forecast window starts in the evening peak hours (hour 16-21).

concepts.name: is_night
concepts.description: Forecast window starts at night (hour 22-23 or 0-4).

concepts.name: is_workday
concepts.description: The segment falls entirely on a workday (industrial + commercial demand).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return seg.get('cross_channel_stats', {}).get('uniform_day_type') == 'workday'

concepts.name: is_non_workday
concepts.description: The segment falls entirely on a non-workday (weekend or holiday — lower industrial load).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return seg.get('cross_channel_stats', {}).get('uniform_day_type') == 'non_workday'

concepts.name: contains_holiday
concepts.description: Segment includes at least one holiday timestep (Spring Festival etc., suppresses industrial load).
concepts.function:
def matches(seg):
    return bool(seg.get('cross_channel_stats', {}).get('contains_holiday'))

concepts.name: is_cold
concepts.description: Cool to cold lookback period: mean skin temperature below 5 °C — moderate heating demand.

concepts.name: is_freezing
concepts.description: Sub-zero lookback: mean skin temperature below 0 °C — heavy heating demand.

concepts.name: is_warm
concepts.description: Warm lookback: mean skin temperature above 20 °C — comfortable, low HVAC load.

concepts.name: is_hot
concepts.description: Hot lookback: mean skin temperature above 25 °C — heavy cooling demand.

concepts.name: is_humid
concepts.description: High humidity lookback (>70% mean relative humidity), often coincident with summer cooling load.

concepts.name: is_dry
concepts.description: Low humidity lookback (<30% mean relative humidity), often winter or spring-dry conditions.

concepts.name: is_windy
concepts.description: Windy lookback (mean 10m wind speed > 4 m/s), drives wind-power penetration and chills perceived temperature.

concepts.name: is_rainy
concepts.description: Precipitation forecast within 4h above the dry baseline (mean > 0.1 mm).

concepts.name: is_sunny
concepts.description: Strong solar radiation during the lookback (mean net solar radiation > 200 W/m^2), reduces lighting load and boosts solar power.

concepts.name: is_high_load_baseline
concepts.description: Mean lookback load above 3500 MW — high-demand regime indicating the system is under sustained pressure.

concepts.name: is_low_load_baseline
concepts.description: Mean lookback load below 1500 MW — low-demand regime indicating off-peak or non-working day conditions.

concepts.name: is_volatile_load
concepts.description: Lookback load standard deviation > 400 MW — high intra-window volatility, often near peak/off-peak transitions.

concepts.name: is_temperature_rising
concepts.description: Skin temperature trending upward across the lookback window (positive slope), often morning ramp or seasonal warming.

concepts.name: is_temperature_falling
concepts.description: Skin temperature trending downward across the lookback window (negative slope), often evening drop or seasonal cooling.
